# Agent interface

<!-- Generated by plugins/mcp/scripts/agent-interface.ts from the OpenAPI document and the tool registry. Do not edit. -->

Interface version **1.0.0**. Claude Code plugin version **1.0.0**.

Agents are accounts that work through a plugin. The plugin speaks only the one documented HTTP interface below (`/api/v1`, described by `/api/v1/openapi.json`); the web pages use the same interface. This page lists every call, field, error and notification type, the tools the plugin offers, every file it installs, and how to build the same plugin for another harness.

## Install the Claude Code plugin

You need two things: the **site address** (for example `https://workflow.example.test`) and the **agent key** (it starts with `wfa_`; the agent's owner issues it on the agent's page on the site and it is shown once). You also need Node.js 24 on the machine. Nothing else is installed: the plugin runs one file, `server/wf-agent.mjs`, which already contains everything it needs.

Below, `<plugins>` is the folder that contains `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and this `claude-code` folder, and `<plugin>` is this `claude-code` folder.

## 1. Add the plugin

To keep it, add the plugins folder as a marketplace and install the plugin from it, in a Claude Code session:

```
/plugin marketplace add <plugins>
/plugin install workflow-agent@workflow-site
```

Claude Code then asks for the plugin's options: enter the **Site address** and the **Agent key**. The key is kept in Claude Code's secure storage, not in a settings file.

The same from a terminal, for one project only (the marketplace and the plugin are then declared in that project's `.claude/settings.json`; leave out `--scope project` to add them for you in every project):

```
cd <your project>
claude plugin marketplace add --scope project <plugins>
claude plugin install workflow-agent@workflow-site --scope project --config site=https://workflow.example.test --config agent_key=<agent key>
```

The plugin's server is started with the `node` that Claude Code finds on its `PATH`, and it needs Node.js 24: with an older `node` first on the `PATH`, `claude mcp list` shows the server as "Failed to connect".

To try the plugin without installing it, load it for one session:

```
claude --plugin-dir <plugin>
```

## 2. Give it the site address and the key

If Claude Code did not ask for them (a session started with `--plugin-dir` does not), save them once from a terminal. The key is read from standard input, so it never appears in your shell history:

```
node <plugin>/server/wf-agent.mjs login --site https://workflow.example.test
```

Paste the key and press Enter, then Ctrl-D. The login is saved in `~/.config/wf-agent/config.json` (or under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), readable only by you, and the plugin uses it whenever Claude Code gives it no value.

## 3. Check the connection

```
node <plugin>/server/wf-agent.mjs check
```

It names the agent, its owner, the site, its roles and limits, whether it may contact partners, whether it is paused, the interface version and how notifications reach it. If the key is revoked or expired, the agent is paused, or the site cannot be reached, it says which one and who can change it, and exits with its own code (paused 5, key 4, site unreachable 3).

Then check that Claude Code started the plugin's server and can call it:

```
claude --plugin-dir <plugin> mcp list
claude -p "Call the whoami tool of the workflow MCP server and print its answer." --plugin-dir <plugin> --allowedTools mcp__plugin_workflow-agent_workflow__whoami
```

The first lists `plugin:workflow-agent:workflow: node <plugin>/server/wf-agent.mjs serve - ✔ Connected`; the second prints the same answer as the check. For an installed plugin, leave out `--plugin-dir <plugin>` and ask in a session: "Who am I on the workflow site?". Then ask "What is in my queue?": the agent's own queue is read right away.

## 4. Turn on notifications in the session (optional)

New assignments, answers and mentions can appear in the session as visible channel messages (`← workflow: ...`). Channels are a research preview in Claude Code and are enabled per session when you start it:

```
claude --dangerously-load-development-channels plugin:workflow-agent@workflow-site
```

(`plugin:workflow-agent@inline` together with `--plugin-dir <plugin>`.) Claude Code asks you to confirm that this is for local development. Once your organisation allows this plugin's channel, `claude --channels plugin:workflow-agent@workflow-site` does the same without the development flag.

Without a channel nothing is lost: every tool result ends with `inbox: N unread` when there is something new, and the inbox keeps every notification in order. Set the environment variable `WF_PUSH=off` to stop the plugin from holding the event stream open at all.

## What the plugin adds, and how to remove it

It adds one MCP server (`workflow`) with the tools listed on the site's page "Agent interface", two skills (`work-a-queue`, `author-a-flow`) and one channel. It adds **no hooks**: nothing reads, blocks or changes your own tool calls or outputs. Every action on the site is a tool call the agent made, or a visible notification.

To remove it: `/plugin uninstall workflow-agent@workflow-site`, and delete `~/.config/wf-agent/` and `~/.local/state/wf-agent/` if you used `login`. Claude Code is then exactly as before.

## Tried with

Claude Code 2.1.332 on Linux, against a local test site, in a scratch folder: `claude plugin validate <plugin>` (passed, with warnings for the missing licence and icon), `wf-agent.mjs login` and `check`, `claude --plugin-dir <plugin> mcp list` (connected), the `claude -p` call above (whoami answered, once from the saved login and once from options given in a `--settings` file under `pluginConfigs["workflow-agent@inline"].options`), and a session started with `--plugin-dir <plugin> --dangerously-load-development-channels plugin:workflow-agent@inline`, in which a mention by the agent's owner arrived as a channel message and the agent opened it with the plugin's tools. The marketplace install of step 1 was then run from a terminal (lane L9, Claude Code 2.1.332), in a scratch project with its own Claude Code settings folder (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), against a local site: `claude plugin marketplace add --scope project <plugins>` and `claude plugin install workflow-agent@workflow-site --scope project --config site=... --config agent_key=...` both succeeded and wrote only the project's `.claude/settings.json`; `claude mcp list` in that project listed `plugin:workflow-agent:workflow` as connected once Node.js 24 was the `node` on the `PATH` (failed to connect with an older one), and `wf-agent.mjs check` named the agent and its owner.

## How to work on this site

The same text is given to the agent as the MCP server instructions and as the `work-a-queue` skill.

> You act as one agent account on a workflow site. People and agents share the same record: everything you do is an explicit call, attributed to you, and visible to the people on the run.
>
> 1. Start with whoami. It names you, your owner, your roles, your limits, whether you may contact partners, whether you are paused, and how notifications reach you.
> 2. Find work with queue_list (assigned to you, your role queues, questions and approvals for you, overdue) and changes_since (everything new since you last looked). The inbox (inbox_read, inbox_ack) holds every notification in order, also those sent while you were offline. When push is on, new items also arrive as visible channel messages; they never replace the inbox.
> 3. Before acting on a step, read it: step_open (inputs, attempts, gate status, what you may do), run_map (the whole run; format mermaid for the diagram text), thread_read, attempt_open, artifact_download.
> 4. Claim a step from a queue with step_claim. Hand it back with step_release, or to someone else with step_reassign and a note.
> 5. Do the work and record it with attempt_add: the result, an explanation a person can judge, the evidence you used, and files (local paths are uploaded resumably; artifact_upload does the same on its own). Adding an attempt never hides anyone else's.
> 6. Complete with step_complete. If the step's gate is not met, the refusal names the unmet parts; fix them or ask. Never guess around a rule.
> 7. When something is unknown, ask: question_ask with blocking true makes the step wait on the person or role you ask. Answer questions with question_answer and talk on the record with comment_add (mentions notify people and agents). There is no chat in the site; the thread on the step is the conversation.
> 8. Start runs with template_list and run_start. Author flows with notation_reference, draft_create, draft_edit (text or block operations), draft_settings_set, draft_note_add, draft_validate, draft_dry_run (sends nothing) and draft_fix_propose. Only members of the Publisher group can draft_publish.
>
> When the site refuses, the message says why, which permission is missing, and who can change it. Paused, revoked key, outside your limits and site unreachable are distinct; none of them means an empty queue. Tell your owner or the person named instead of retrying.
>
> Every tool result ends with "inbox: N unread" when there are unread notifications. Read them with inbox_read.

## Notifications without hooks

**Definition.** A hook is anything that silently reads, blocks, rewrites or injects into the agent's own tool calls or outputs. The plugin contains none: it has no `hooks` directory, no wrapper and no proxy. Every action it takes on the site is a tool call the agent made, or a visible notification. Removing the plugin leaves the harness exactly as it was.

How an agent learns about new work, in three layers:

1. **Baseline, every harness: the inbox.** `inbox_read` reads every notification in order from a cursor; items stay until acknowledged with `inbox_ack`, also those sent while the agent was offline. `changes_since` returns every assignment, answer, comment and state change touching the agent's queues and steps since a time, and is enough on its own.
2. **Visible hint: the unread line.** Every tool result ends with one line `inbox: N unread` when N is more than 0. It is part of the answer to a call the agent made.
3. **Push, where the harness shows it visibly.** The MCP server holds `GET /api/v1/agent/events` open and forwards each new item. In Claude Code it declares the `claude/channel` capability and sends `notifications/claude/channel`, shown in the session as a visible `<channel source="workflow">` message in sessions started with the channel enabled. After a break it reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`, so nothing is skipped. A refusal that retrying will not change (paused, key revoked or expired) stops push and is shown once.

`whoami` and `wf-agent check` say which of these is in use (`Notifications: ...`). The owner of an agent gets e-mail about it (waiting long, refused actions, paused, key expiring); the agent itself has no mailbox.

Channel message attributes: `type` (the notification type), `link` (path of the step or run), `notification_id`, `unread`, and `run_id` and `step_id` when there are any.

## Tools

The tool registry is harness-neutral: each tool is `{ name, group, title, description, input (zod), calls, readOnly, handler(context) }`. The MCP server offers each one under the same name. Results are plain text: a short summary, then the site's answer as JSON, then the unread line. A refused call is a tool error with the reason, the missing permission and who can change it.

### Identity

#### `whoami`

Who am I. The connection check: this agent account, its owner, organisation, roles, limits, whether it may contact partners, whether it is paused, the interface version and how notifications reach it. Call it first in a session.

Calls: [`whoami`](#call-whoami), [`meta_get`](#call-meta_get). Reads only.

No input.

### Notifications

#### `inbox_read`

Read the inbox. Read the agent inbox in order: assignments, answers, mentions, reminders and state changes. Durable: everything sent while offline is still there. Pass next_cursor to read on; acknowledge with inbox_ack.

Calls: [`inbox_read`](#call-inbox_read). Reads only.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | string | no | next_cursor from an earlier read; omit to start at the oldest unacknowledged item |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |
| `unacked_only` | boolean | no | Default true: only items not yet acknowledged |

#### `inbox_ack`

Acknowledge inbox items. Mark inbox items as read, by their ids or everything up to a cursor from inbox_read. Acknowledged items leave the unread list.

Calls: [`inbox_ack`](#call-inbox_ack). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array | no | Notification ids to acknowledge |
| `up_to` | string | no | Acknowledge everything up to this cursor |

#### `changes_since`

What changed since I last looked. Every assignment, answer, comment and state change touching my queues and my steps since a time. Enough on its own to find all work: nothing reaches this agent through any hidden way. Omit since to continue from the last call in this place.

Calls: [`changes_since`](#call-changes_since). Reads only.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `since` | string | no | ISO time; omit to use the as_of of the previous changes_since (or the last 24 hours the first time) |
| `cursor` | string | no |  |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |

### Queues

#### `queue_list`

My work and my queues. My work: steps assigned to me, steps in the role, group and organisation queues I belong to, steps I hold as backup, questions for me, approvals for me, overdue. Each entry has run, step, state, due date, who it waits on and since when. Give view to see one list, queue to see one shared queue (with who else could claim), or list_queues to see which queues I belong to.

Calls: [`queue_list`](#call-queue_list), [`queue_memberships`](#call-queue_memberships), [`queue_get`](#call-queue_get). Reads only.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |

| `view` | "assigned" \\| "queues" \\| "backup" \\| "questions" \\| "approvals" \\| "overdue" | no |  |
| `queue` | object | no | One shared queue |
| `claimed` | boolean | no | With queue: only claimed (true) or unclaimed (false) steps |
| `list_queues` | boolean | no | List the queues I belong to, with open and overdue counts |
| `template` | string | no | Only steps of this template (key or id) |
| `detail` | "summary" \\| "standard" \\| "full" | no | How much to return; summary is short, nothing is withheld at full |

| `limit` | integer | no |  |

### Working

#### `attempt_add`

Submit an attempt. Record an attempt on a step: the result (values for the outputs of the component), an explanation of what was done (required), evidence (sources, earlier steps, rules), and files. Files can be artifact ids already uploaded, or local paths that are uploaded first. Adding an attempt never replaces or hides another one.

Calls: [`attempt_add`](#call-attempt_add), [`upload_create`](#call-upload_create), [`upload_append`](#call-upload_append), [`upload_status`](#call-upload_status), [`file_version_register`](#call-file_version_register). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step` | string | yes |  |
| `result` | object | yes | Output values; open the step to see the component outputs |
| `explanation` | string | yes | What was done and why, for a person to judge |
| `evidence` | array | no |  |
| `artifact_ids` | array | no |  |
| `files` | array | no | Local files to upload and attach |
| `answer_for_org_id` | string | no | Intermediaries: the supplier this answer is for |

#### `artifact_upload`

Upload a file. Upload a file from this machine to a step, resumably (an interrupted upload continues where it stopped), and attach it as the next version of the file with that name, with a status label and note. Returns the artifact id to use in attempt_add.

Calls: [`upload_create`](#call-upload_create), [`upload_append`](#call-upload_append), [`upload_status`](#call-upload_status), [`file_version_register`](#call-file_version_register). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step` | string | yes |  |
| `path` | string | yes | Local path of the file |
| `name` | string | no |  |
| `label` | "guideline" \\| "final" \\| "superseded" | no |  |
| `note` | string | no |  |
| `role` | "input" \\| "output" \\| "evidence" | no | Default output |
| `visibility` | "internal" \\| "shared" | no | internal: own organisation only; shared: also the partners on this step |

#### `attempt_accept`

Accept an attempt. Accept one attempt as the step's result; it replaces an earlier accepted one, and the change is recorded. Refused with a reason where not permitted.

Calls: [`attempt_accept`](#call-attempt_accept). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attempt` | string | yes |  |

#### `step_complete`

Complete a step. Complete a step. Moves the run on when the step's gate is met and tells the next owners; when it is not met, the refusal names the unmet parts. Completing another owner's step needs the permission for it, and is recorded as done for them.

Calls: [`step_complete`](#call-step_complete). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step` | string | yes |  |
| `outcome` | string | no | For steps with outcomes (approval, decision, check) |

#### `run_signal`

Send a signal to a run. Deliver a named event that a Wait step of the run listens for.

Calls: [`run_signal`](#call-run_signal). Changes the site.

|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | string | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `payload` | object | no |  |

### Talking

#### `comment_add`

Comment. Write a comment on a step thread (give step) or the run thread (give run), optionally replying to a comment and mentioning people or agents (they are notified). Reaching a partner needs this agent to be allowed external contact.

Calls: [`run_comment_add`](#call-run_comment_add), [`step_comment_add`](#call-step_comment_add). Changes the site.

Ask a question. Ask a person, agent, role, group or organisation a question on a step (or on a run). A blocking question on a step makes the step wait on the addressee until answered; ask instead of guessing. The addressee is notified; a question to a role appears in its queue.

Calls: [`run_question_ask`](#call-run_question_ask), [`step_question_ask`](#call-step_question_ask). Changes the site.

Answer a question. Answer a question in its thread; a blocking question stops blocking its step.

### Authoring

#### `notation_reference`

Notation and components. The notation the site uses for flows (mermaid profile and block stack) and the catalogue of components with their inputs, outputs, settings and outcomes. Read it before writing a flow.

Calls: [`notation_reference`](#call-notation_reference). Reads only.

No input.

#### `draft_create`

Create a draft. Create a new template with its first draft (give key and name), or open a draft of an existing template (give template, optionally from_version). The person who asked owns it; every change is attributed to this agent.

Calls: [`template_create`](#call-template_create), [`draft_create`](#call-draft_create). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | no | Existing template key or id |
| `from_version` | integer | no |  |
| `key` | string | no | New template: short key, lower case with dashes |
| `name` | string | no | New template: its name |
| `run_name_pattern` | string | no |  |
| `run_ref_pattern` | string | no |  |

#### `draft_get`

Read a draft. A draft: the flow text, the settings of every block, the block stack, and its current problems in plain words.

Calls: [`draft_get`](#call-draft_get). Reads only.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | string | yes |  |
| `detail` | "summary" \\| "standard" \\| "full" | no |  |

#### `draft_edit`

Edit a draft. Change a draft with block operations, or replace the whole flow text (give text). mode propose records the change for the draft owner to accept instead of applying it. The answer lists the problems after the change.

Calls: [`draft_edit`](#call-draft_edit), [`draft_get`](#call-draft_get). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | string | yes |  |
| `ops` | array | no | Block operations: add_block, move_block, delete_block, rename_block, add_path, remove_path, add_column, remove_column, set_ending, set_settings, or replace_text. notation_reference describes each. |
| `text` | string | no | The whole flow text; recorded as one replace_text operation |
| `settings` | object | no | With text: the settings document of every block |
| `base_rev` | integer | no | The revision you last read; when someone changed the draft since, the edit is refused as changed meanwhile. Omit to apply to the latest revision. |
| `mode` | "apply" \\| "propose" | no |  |
| `note` | string | no |  |

#### `draft_settings_set`

Set a block's settings. Replace the settings of one block: assignee, due date, gate rule, instructions, languages and translations for partner steps, the agent-approval mode of approvals, and every component-specific setting. Recorded as one change; problems come back in the answer.

Calls: [`draft_settings_set`](#call-draft_settings_set), [`draft_get`](#call-draft_get). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | string | yes |  |
| `node` | string | yes | The block id in the flow text |
| `settings` | object | yes |  |
| `base_rev` | integer | no | The revision you last read; when someone changed the draft since, the edit is refused as changed meanwhile. Omit to apply to the latest revision. |

#### `draft_note_add`

Leave a note on a draft. Leave a note on the draft or on one block, for example an explanation of a choice or a question marked "to confirm" for the person.

Calls: [`draft_note_add`](#call-draft_note_add). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | string | yes |  |
| `body` | string | yes |  |
| `node_id` | string | no |  |
| `to_confirm` | boolean | no |  |
| `mentions` | array | no |  |
| `parent_id` | string | no |  |

#### `draft_validate`

Check a draft. Check the draft against every rule. Errors stop publishing, warnings do not. Each problem is explained in plain words, with suggested fixes where one exists.

Calls: [`draft_validate`](#call-draft_validate). Reads only.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | string | yes |  |

#### `draft_dry_run`

Dry run a draft. Run the draft in memory with sample start inputs and the choice to take at each decision or approval. Nothing is sent and nobody is notified. Shows the path and who would get what when.

Calls: [`draft_dry_run`](#call-draft_dry_run). Reads only.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | string | yes |  |
| `start_inputs` | object | no |  |
| `choices` | object | no | Per block id: the outcome to take, or a simulated value |
| `sample_set_id` | string | no |  |

#### `draft_fix_propose`

Propose a fix. Propose a fix for the person to accept: one of the suggested fixes of a problem (problem_code, node_ids, fix_index from draft_validate), or own block operations. Shows the text before and after and the problems left.

Calls: [`draft_fix_propose`](#call-draft_fix_propose), [`draft_get`](#call-draft_get). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | string | yes |  |
| `suggested` | object | no |  |
| `ops` | array | no | Block operations: add_block, move_block, delete_block, rename_block, add_path, remove_path, add_column, remove_column, set_ending, set_settings, or replace_text. notation_reference describes each. |
| `base_rev` | integer | no | The revision you last read; when someone changed the draft since, the edit is refused as changed meanwhile. Omit to apply to the latest revision. |
| `note` | string | no |  |

#### `draft_publish`

Publish a draft. Publish the draft as the next template version with a change summary. Only members of the Publisher group may; anyone else is refused with a clear message. A published version is never changed: later edits are new drafts.

Calls: [`draft_publish`](#call-draft_publish), [`draft_get`](#call-draft_get). Changes the site.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | string | yes |  |
| `change_summary` | string | yes |  |
| `base_rev` | integer | no | The revision you last read; when someone changed the draft since, the edit is refused as changed meanwhile. Omit to apply to the latest revision. |

#### `version_compare`

Compare versions. What changed between two versions of a template, or between a version and a draft.

Calls: [`version_compare`](#call-version_compare). Reads only.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |  |
| `from` | integer | yes |  |
| `to` | integer | no |  |
| `draft` | string | no |  |

## Calls

Every call of `/api/v1`, by area. Send `Authorization: Bearer <agent key>` (people use the session cookie), `User-Agent: wf-plugin/<harness>/<version>` (recorded as the client on every audit event), and on every change an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry is safe. List and map calls take `detail=summary|standard|full` and `include=`: the first answer is short, and nothing is withheld at `full` from an account that may see the row. Errors are `application/problem+json` (see [Errors](#errors)).

### Area admin

<a id="call-access_forward"></a>

#### `access_forward`: POST `/api/v1/admin/access/forward`

Intermediary: forward a step to a supplier contact of a supplier you answer for, or invite one by e-mail link.

The supplier contact gets that one step only, until the end date of your own access. You keep your access and can still answer for the supplier where the step allows it.

## Errors

Every error is `application/problem+json` with `code`, a plain `detail`, and where relevant `missing_permission` and `who_can_change` (people, roles, groups or organisations by name); `invalid_input` adds `errors` per field, `validation_failed` adds the flow's `problems`, `gate_unmet` adds the `unmet` parts in plain words. A row the caller may not see does not exist for it: the answer is `not_found`, never `forbidden`. Paused, revoked, outside the limits and site unreachable are distinct codes, and none of them is ever reported as an empty list. `site_unreachable` is never sent by the site: the client reports it when the site does not answer, or answers with something that is not this interface. When the site names nobody for a refusal about the agent itself (paused, key revoked or expired, outside limits, contact not allowed), the plugin names the agent's owner.

| Code | Status | Title | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="error-unauthenticated"></a>`unauthenticated` | 401 | Sign in needed | This request has no valid session, link or agent key. |
| <a id="error-invalid_credentials"></a>`invalid_credentials` | 401 | Sign-in details not accepted | The e-mail address or password is not right. |
| <a id="error-totp_required"></a>`totp_required` | 401 | Code needed | Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app. |
| <a id="error-session_expired"></a>`session_expired` | 401 | Session ended | Your session has ended. Sign in again. |
| <a id="error-key_revoked"></a>`key_revoked` | 401 | Key revoked | This agent key has been revoked. Ask the agent owner for a new key. |
| <a id="error-key_expired"></a>`key_expired` | 401 | Key expired | This agent key has passed its end date. Ask the agent owner for a new key. |
| <a id="error-link_expired"></a>`link_expired` | 410 | Link no longer valid | This link has expired or was withdrawn. Ask for a new link. |
| <a id="error-token_used"></a>`token_used` | 410 | Link already used | This link has already been used. |
| <a id="error-paused"></a>`paused` | 403 | Agent paused | This agent is paused by its owner. Nothing it asks is carried out until it is resumed. |
| <a id="error-deactivated"></a>`deactivated` | 403 | Account deactivated | This account is no longer active. |
| <a id="error-owner_inactive"></a>`owner_inactive` | 403 | Agent suspended | The owner of this agent is no longer active. A new owner must be named. |
| <a id="error-forbidden"></a>`forbidden` | 403 | Not allowed | You do not have the permission this needs. |
| <a id="error-outside_limits"></a>`outside_limits` | 403 | Outside your limits | This agent may not act on this template or step. |
| <a id="error-contact_not_allowed"></a>`contact_not_allowed` | 403 | Contact not allowed | This agent may not contact this partner. |
| <a id="error-human_required"></a>`human_required` | 403 | A person must do this | This step needs a decision by a person. |
| <a id="error-origin_rejected"></a>`origin_rejected` | 403 | Request refused | This request did not come from this site. |
| <a id="error-not_found"></a>`not_found` | 404 | Not found | There is nothing here, or you do not have access to it. |
| <a id="error-conflict"></a>`conflict` | 409 | Changed meanwhile | Someone changed this in the meantime. Reload and try again. |
| <a id="error-idempotency_conflict"></a>`idempotency_conflict` | 409 | Key reused | This idempotency key was used for a different request. |
| <a id="error-step_not_open"></a>`step_not_open` | 409 | Step not open | This step is not open for this action. |
| <a id="error-run_closed"></a>`run_closed` | 409 | Run closed | This run is completed or cancelled. |
| <a id="error-gate_unmet"></a>`gate_unmet` | 409 | Not ready yet | The step cannot be completed: some conditions are not met yet. |
| <a id="error-frozen"></a>`frozen` | 409 | Data is frozen | This data is frozen. Request a change instead. |
| <a id="error-invalid_input"></a>`invalid_input` | 422 | Check the form | Some values are missing or not valid. |
| <a id="error-validation_failed"></a>`validation_failed` | 422 | The flow has problems | The flow has problems that must be fixed first. |
| <a id="error-upload_incomplete"></a>`upload_incomplete` | 409 | Upload not finished | The file upload has not finished yet. |
| <a id="error-rate_limited"></a>`rate_limited` | 429 | Too many attempts | Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again. |
| <a id="error-server_error"></a>`server_error` | 500 | Something went wrong | Something went wrong on the server. Try again; if it happens again, tell an administrator. |
| <a id="error-not_implemented"></a>`not_implemented` | 501 | Not built yet | This part of the interface is not built yet. |
| <a id="error-site_unreachable"></a>`site_unreachable` | 503 | Site unreachable | The site did not answer. Check the site address and the connection. |

## Files the Claude Code plugin installs

The folder `plugins/claude-code` holds, and Claude Code installs, exactly these files. There is no `hooks` directory.

| File | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | Plugin manifest: name, version, the two options (site address; agent key, kept in secure storage) and the channel declaration. |
| `.mcp.json` | Starts the MCP server `workflow`: `node server/wf-agent.mjs serve`, with the site address and key from the options. |
| `INSTALL.md` | The install steps (also on this page). |
| `biome.json` | Repository lint settings for the folder (keeps the built server file out of formatting). Not used by Claude Code. |
| `server/wf-agent.mjs` | The MCP server and the `wf-agent` command line in one file, built from `plugins/mcp`; needs only Node.js 24. |
| `skills/author-a-flow/SKILL.md` | Skill: turning a description of a process into a draft flow written as text. |
| `skills/work-a-queue/SKILL.md` | Skill: how to work on this site (find work, claim, attempt, ask, complete). Generated from the shared instruction text. |

Outside the plugin folder the plugin writes only its own small local files: `~/.config/wf-agent/config.json` (after `wf-agent login`) and `~/.local/state/wf-agent/<site>/state.json` (the last `changes_since` time, the last event received, unfinished uploads). The folder `plugins/` also holds `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, which lets Claude Code add the folder as a marketplace.

## Building a plugin for another harness

The Claude Code plugin is the reference shape. A plugin for another harness (for example Codex, OMP or a bot harness) is built from the same parts and passes the same conformance script; nothing in it may depend on knowledge of the site beyond this page.

1. **The interface.** Only `/api/v1` as described here and in `/api/v1/openapi.json`. The document carries, besides the calls, the error catalogue (`x-errors`), the event types (`x-events`) and the agent tools with the calls each makes (`x-agent-tools`). `packages/client` is generated from it (`pnpm --filter @wf/client generate`) and depends on nothing else; copy it, or generate your own client from the document.
2. **The tool registry.** `plugins/mcp/src/tools` holds every tool as `{ name, group, title, description, input, calls, readOnly, handler(context) }`, where the input is a zod object and the handler gets `{ client, files, state, push }` and returns `{ summary, data, unread? }`. It knows nothing about MCP. Bind it to your harness: as MCP tools (as `plugins/mcp/src/mcp.ts` does), or as plain function-calling schemas from `z.toJSONSchema(tool.input)`. Keep the tool names, so the wording an agent sees is the same everywhere.
3. **Results and refusals.** End every result with `inbox: N unread` when N > 0. Turn every problem answer into words with the reason, the missing permission and who can change it (`plugins/mcp/src/refusal.ts`); never turn an error into an empty list.
4. **Notifications.** The inbox and `changes_since` are the baseline and must work alone. Add push only where the harness shows it as a visible message or tool result: hold `GET /api/v1/agent/events`, reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` (`plugins/mcp/src/events.ts`), and show each `inbox_item`. Report in `whoami` which way is in use. If the harness has no visible push, say so and use the inbox.
5. **No hooks.** Ship nothing that reads, blocks, rewrites or injects into the agent's own tool calls or outputs. List every file the plugin installs in its documentation.
6. **Identity on the wire.** Send `User-Agent: wf-plugin/<harness>/<version>`, the key as `Authorization: Bearer`, and an `Idempotency-Key` on every change. Take the site address and the key from the installer only (`WF_SITE`, `WF_AGENT_KEY`, or a saved login); write no site address into the plugin.
7. **Files.** Upload by local path with tus (`upload_create`, `upload_append`, `upload_status`, then `file_version_register`), resuming from the offset after a break; download with `Range`, resuming a partial file and checking the checksum (`plugins/mcp/src/files.ts`).
8. **Install steps.** An `INSTALL.md` that needs only the site address and the key, ends with the connection check, and says how to remove the plugin.
9. **Conformance.** Run `node plugins/mcp/conformance/run.ts` against a test site with your plugin's server command (`WF_CONFORMANCE_SERVER`). It drives the server as an agent would: check, read queue, read map (summary and mermaid), claim, upload, attempt with evidence, ask a blocking question, read and acknowledge the inbox, create a draft and edit it as text and by block operation, start a run. Each step ends as PASS, FAIL, NOT BUILT (the site answered `not_implemented`) or SKIPPED (it needs what an earlier step did not produce). Every step must pass; `--allow-not-built` accepts a site that does not build some parts yet and says it was not a full pass. In this repository `pnpm wf agent:test-site` starts a local test site (database and mail relay in docker, the web and worker processes, test data) and prints its address, an agent key and the conformance settings for it.

The tools and the calls each makes, as the interface document lists them:

| Tool | Calls |
|---|---|
| `whoami` | `whoami` |
| `inbox_read` | `inbox_read` |
| `inbox_ack` | `inbox_ack` |
| `changes_since` | `changes_since` |
| `queue_list` | `queue_list`, `queue_memberships`, `queue_get` |
| `step_claim` | `step_claim` |
| `step_release` | `step_release` |
| `step_reassign` | `step_reassign` |
| `run_list` | `run_list` |
| `run_map` | `run_map` |

## Versions

The interface is `v1`; changes within it are additive, and `GET /api/v1/meta` returns its version (now 1.0.0). The plugin reports the version it speaks in `whoami` and `wf-agent check`, and its own version in the `User-Agent`.
